- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After a price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct downward quickly — overcorrecting or lagging mean reversion.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, particularly when true values show a downward trend or mean reversion.
- Forecast bias is more pronounced when historical prices are volatile or show recent sharp moves.
- Model exhibits persistent lag in responding to recent price drops — often underestimating the depth of a correction.
- When true prices are clustered near a recent low, model tends to overestimate the continuation of that low, missing the rebound.
- Model is sensitive to recent high prices — overreacting to short-term spikes and failing to adjust for longer-term mean reversion.
- Forecast accuracy improves when model incorporates a 3–5 day moving average of recent prices as a smoothing filter.
- Model should reduce forecast magnitude when true prices show a clear downward trend in the last 7–10 days.
- Avoid overfitting to recent spikes — model should not extrapolate upward beyond 2–3 standard deviations above recent mean.
